description: We're The Moonies 🌙.A team excited to make space exploration fun and interactive for young learners! We’re interested in software development, AI/ML, and creative problem-solving. We're looking for teammates with skills in game development, UI/UX, Python, or space science who want to share ideas, learn together, and build an engaging astronaut mission simulator.
summary:
Mission Moonbase is an interactive educational lunar survival simulation designed to introduce young learners to the challenges of establishing and sustaining a human presence on the Moon.

The project allows players to take command of a crew of four astronauts on a 30-day lunar mission. Players configure their mission, select essential equipment, construct a lunar outpost and manage critical resources such as oxygen, water, food and energy. As the mission progresses, they encounter unexpected events, including space-weather hazards, and must make decisions that affect crew safety and mission success.

Beyond gameplay, Mission Moonbase incorporates educational content explaining lunar science, life-support systems, radiation protection, resource management and In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU). Through interactive decision-making and mission debriefs, it helps learners understand the scientific and engineering challenges of future lunar exploration.
details:
Project Details

Mission Moonbase: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive educational lunar survival simulation designed to introduce young learners to the scientific, technological and engineering challenges of establishing a sustainable human presence on the Moon.

The project places players in command of a crew of four astronauts undertaking a 30-day lunar expedition. Rather than simply presenting information about space exploration, it allows players to experience the challenges through interactive decisions and resource management.

How It Works

The simulation guides players through different stages of a lunar mission. It begins with a mission briefing and a Science Primer that introduces important concepts related to lunar conditions, radiation, thermal cycles and In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU).

Players then configure their mission, select a landing location, choose their crew and select essential equipment while considering mission requirements and payload constraints. Using their selected equipment, they construct a lunar outpost before beginning the operational phase.

During the mission, players monitor and manage four critical resources: oxygen, water, food and energy. They must also monitor crew conditions and respond to unexpected mission events, including space-weather hazards. Their decisions influence resource availability, crew safety and overall mission performance. At the end, a mission debrief provides an evaluation of their decisions and highlights important learning outcomes.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Mission Moonbase makes complex space science and engineering concepts more accessible through interactive learning. It encourages learners to think critically, solve problems, manage limited resources and understand the consequences of engineering decisions.

The project aims to:

  • Improve awareness of lunar exploration and future human missions.
  • Introduce the importance of life-support systems and resource sustainability.
  • Explain radiation protection and space-weather hazards.
  • Encourage interest in STEM education through simulation-based learning.
  • Help young learners understand the challenges of building and maintaining extraterrestrial habitats.

Technology Used

The project was developed as a web-based application using:

  • React: Building the interactive user interface and application components.
  • Vite: Development and build environment.
  • JavaScript: Implementing mission interactions and simulation logic.
  • Tailwind CSS: Styling and responsive interface design.
  • Framer Motion: Adding animations and interactive transitions.
  • Lucide React: Interface icons.
  • Recharts: Visual representation of mission resources and data.
  • LocalStorage: Maintaining relevant mission data within the browser.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of Mission Moonbase lies in transforming lunar exploration into a decision-driven learning experience. Instead of limiting the experience to static educational content, the project allows learners to take responsibility for an entire simulated mission.

The combination of mission configuration, equipment selection, outpost construction, resource monitoring, dynamic events and mission evaluation creates a connected learning experience. Players can understand how individual decisions affect the wider mission, making scientific concepts easier to explore and remember.

Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered several important factors while developing the project:

  • Educational accessibility: Keeping the experience understandable and engaging for young learners.
  • Scientific relevance: Including realistic challenges associated with lunar exploration and human survival.
  • Resource limitations: Representing the importance of managing finite supplies during long-duration missions.
  • Decision-making: Ensuring that player choices have consequences for mission progress and crew safety.
  • User experience: Designing an interactive interface that makes different mission stages easy to navigate.
  • Learning outcomes: Combining gameplay with scientific explanations and a final mission debrief.

Through Mission Moonbase, we aim to inspire the next generation of explorers by helping them understand that successful lunar exploration involves not only reaching the Moon, but also developing the knowledge and technology needed to survive there sustainably.
